references.text: Abraham was asked to offer his son Isaac as a burnt offering, which shows the parallel to Jephthah's vow to offer whatever came out of his house first
The law concerning vows dedicated to the Lord that cannot be revoked, which may shed light on Jephthah's understanding of his vow
Rules about vows made to the Lord and the importance of keeping what one has promised
The command to keep vows given to the Lord without hesitation
The warning not to be hasty in making vows to God and the importance of fulfilling them
Hannah's vow to give her son to the Lord, another example of a vow to give something dear to God
The fulfillment of Jephthah's vow when his daughter came out to meet him
Jephthah is mentioned among the heroes of faith who by faith conquered their enemies
